## Current Work at YAGNI (yagni.app)

YAGNI builds agent teams for engineering organizations ("Agent teams, managed like your engineering team"). Named AI agents (a builder, a reviewer, a product manager and others) work like a real engineering team, taking software work from a proposal to a merged pull request under a plan that a human approves. Every important step leaves a record a person can review, and autonomy is earned through a track record. YAGNI integrates with the tools the team already uses (GitHub first) and doesn't replace them.

### Focus Areas & Key Contributions at YAGNI
1. **Multi-Tenant Isolation & Sandboxed Execution**: Hardened multi-tenant data access by closing cross-customer data exposure paths in the operator API, enforcing tenant-scoped query guards, and hardening the sandboxed code runner.
2. **Code-Review Agent Reliability & Evaluation**: Fixed ticket-key collisions between YAGNI and external trackers that routed the reviewer agent to the wrong issue; built realistic evaluation benchmarks modeled on customer work to measure whether changes make agents better or worse.
3. **Self-Healing Syncs & Observability**: Made connector backfills self-healing (stuck-cursor recovery, progress tracking, hard caps for large external workspaces) and built stalled-run detection + an early-warning "risk radar".
4. **Self-Improving Agents & Monorepo DX**: Built an experimental system where agents review failed runs, find root causes, and propose fixes; streamlined the monorepo build chain so a fresh checkout, worktree, or CI run builds its dependencies with a single command.
5. **Customer Pilots**: Technical point of contact for pilot customers in the time zone — troubleshooting, running demos, and turning customer feedback into engineering work.

### How I Work
I build with AI agents every day: I plan, delegate to agents, review their output with a second "judge" agent, and keep the human decision where it matters.
